title: From the National Minimum Wage to the Anthony Albanese Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Compare the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and even the Anthony Albanese salary to under
salarySummary: To convert an hourly rate to annual salary, multiply by hours per week (usually 38) and then by 52 weeks, giving a gross annual figure before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee on 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour yields $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. When using our timesheet, check the casual loading box to add this automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $52,245 annual salary, your employer would contribute an extra $6,269.40 into your super fund. This is not included in your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual

Whether you're negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or just curious about your annual worth, converting an hourly rate to a yearly figure is a straightforward calculation. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = gross annual salary**

For most full-time employees, the assumed work week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission. This is the basis for the National Minimum Wage and many award classifications. If you work part-time or casual, your weekly hours may differ, but the formula remains the same.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. This applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. However, most Australian workers are covered by an award, which sets minimum pay rates higher than the National Minimum Wage. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026.

For example, a retail employee under the General Retail Industry Award may earn a higher base rate than the National Minimum Wage. To check your specific award rate, use the [pay guides](/blog) on our site or the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool.

### Casual Loading: What It Means for Your Pay

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave or sick leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [timesheet](/), you can check the "casual loading" box to automatically add this 25% to your base rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading—the tool handles it for you.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage, that's $1,004.90 × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight**. This can help when budgeting or comparing salary packages.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum earnings base for super contributions is $270,830 per year. For example, on an annual salary of $52,245, your employer would contribute an extra $6,269.40. This is not included in your take-home pay but is a valuable part of your total remuneration package.

### Tax: What You'll Actually Take Home

Your gross annual salary is not what lands in your bank account. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Using our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator, you can see how much of your gross salary remains after tax and Medicare.

### The Anthony Albanese Salary: A Point of Comparison

To put these figures in perspective, consider the **Anthony Albanese salary**. As Prime Minister, his base salary is set by the Remuneration Tribunal and is significantly higher than award or minimum wage rates. While the exact figure changes with annual determinations, it serves as a reminder of the wide range of pay in Australia. Most workers earn far less, and understanding your own hourly-to-annual conversion is the first step to knowing your worth. Whether you're on the National Minimum Wage or a higher award rate, the same formula applies: hourly × hours per week × 52.

### Using Our Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and instantly see your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay. You can also toggle casual loading. For more detailed comparisons, visit our [reference tables](/data) which include award rates, ABS Average Weekly Earnings, and tax brackets.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is simple: multiply by your weekly hours and then by 52. For most full-time workers, that's 38 hours per week. Whether you're comparing the National Minimum Wage, an award rate, or even the Anthony Albanese salary, the formula is the same. Use our tools to get a clear picture of your gross pay, super, and estimated tax.
